title: Cross-Border River Ecology, The Hague Judgment and Environmental Movements

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: The 1977 Czechoslovak-Hungarian treaty on the Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros dam catalyzed the Hungarian democratic opposition: the *Duna Kör* organized massive protest against ecological destruction. In 1989 Hungary suspended construction, prompting Slovakia's 1992 unilateral diversion of the Danube (*C-variáns*).

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: The 1997 International Court of Justice judgment found that both sides had breached their obligations (Hungary in suspending and abandoning works, Slovakia in putting the diversion into operation) and told them to negotiate in good faith.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A Duna egyoldalú elterelése jelentősen lecsökkentette a Szigetköz vízhozamát.
Unilateral diversion of the Danube greatly reduced the water discharge of the Szigetköz.
A Duna Kör fellépése a rendszerváltás előtti ellenzéki mozgalmak egyik fontos színterévé vált.
The action of the Danube Circle became one important arena of the opposition movements before the change of regime.
A hágai perben mindkét felet elmarasztalták a szerződés megsértéséért.
In the Hague lawsuit both parties were censured for breach of treaty.
